S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving an installed battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 30 days. The manufacturer must notify the affected customer within 72 hours, with immediate notice where there is an urgent safety risk.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving an installed battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 30 days. The manufacturer must notify the affected customer within 72 hours, with immediate notice where there is an urgent safety risk. Reports must include known injuries, property damage, and containment actions; suspected incidents must not be omitted pending confirmation.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55°C before market entry and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. Beginning 24 months after this standard takes effect, a model’s failure rate must not exceed 7%.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55°C before market entry and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective actions to the regulator. Regulators must protect precise per-model results from general public disclosure. Before purchase, customers and prospective customers must receive the test date, sample size, and precise per-model failure rate, together with a clear explanation of material findings and safety implications. Beginning 24 months after this standard takes effect, a model’s failure rate must not exceed 7%. A model exceeding the limit must promptly submit a corrective-action plan and retest within 12 months; regulators may require interim safeguards, restrict sales, or take other protective measures based on the evidence. Manufacturers must promptly inform regulators and affected customers of material changes or newly identified safety risks.

parameters.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years of the standard’s effective date, where technically feasible.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years of the standard’s effective date, where technically feasible.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years of the standard’s effective date, where technically feasible. Manufacturers must provide customers with clear instructions for activating the feature and disclose any units that cannot be retrofitted.

parameters.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide regulators with evidence of compliance and disclose to customers whether the unit includes the required system.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide regulators with evidence of compliance and disclose to customers whether the unit includes the required system.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide regulators with evidence of compliance and disclose to customers whether the unit includes the required system.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices about incidents affecting their model, known risks, and recommended precautions or corrective actions, promptly and no later than 72 hours after notifying regulators, with immediate notice for urgent risks. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting model-specific data, and the manufacturer must initiate a recall and promptly notify affected customers with instructions and remedies.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices about incidents affecting their model, known risks, and recommended precautions or corrective actions, promptly and no later than 72 hours after notifying regulators, with immediate notice for urgent risks. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting model-specific data, and the manufacturer must initiate a recall and promptly notify affected customers with instructions and remedies.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices about incidents affecting their model, known risks, and recommended precautions or corrective actions, promptly and no later than 72 hours after notifying regulators, with immediate notice for urgent risks. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting model-specific data, and the manufacturer must initiate a recall and promptly notify affected customers with instructions and remedies. The regulator may require additional protective measures. The trigger is model-specific; company-wide rates do not establish that a model has crossed it.

This keeps the trigger meaningful without making recall automatic regardless of evidence.

judge_section_notes: S1 adopts strict 24-hour reporting for any thermal incident, 72-hour customer notice, and explicitly disallows omitting suspected incidents pending confirmation. S2 sets a 55°C test and a 7% failure limit after a 24-month phase-in, with precise per-model rates given to customers but protected from public disclosure. S3 requires new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit deadline where technically feasible, S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months, and S5 mandates recall above a model-specific 8/100k trigger with 72-hour safety notices.
